name: koalafix
description: One memory for every AI tool on your team. Facts show who checked them and when.

interface.shortDescription: Team memory for your AI tools
interface.longDescription:
KoalaFix is one shared memory for a software team that uses more than one AI tool. ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI and other MCP clients connect to the same hosted server, so a note saved from one tool can be recalled from any other.

What you can do from ChatGPT or Codex:
- Recall memory. Ask what your team already knows. You get a verdict first (clear, stale, conflict or unknown), then the facts, notes and what teammates are working on.
- Remember a note. Record a decision, rule or fact for your team under a name, so your teammates' assistants see it. A new value under the same name becomes the current one, and the earlier value stays in its history.
- Verify a fact. Mark that you checked a fact's source and it still holds, or record the new value.
- Track work. Claim a task before you start and see whether a teammate is on overlapping work. Finish it, or hand it over to a teammate.
- List open items. What is waiting on you or the team, who owns it and how it closes.
- Settle an item. Retire a note, dismiss an item, pass it to its owner, undo, resolve a disagreement once you have decided, or erase a note for good.
- Share to the team. Copy one of your private notes to the team when you ask. Teammates can read the copy straight away.
- Save a new note. Keep a private note that only you can see. It only adds: nothing already saved is changed.
- Search help pages and Read a help page. Answer "how do I..." questions about KoalaFix itself from its own docs.

Every fact carries a sticker: who checked it and when. An answer checked ten minutes ago looks different from one nobody has looked at since last month. When two people save different values, the one with more standing on the team wins, a lower-standing value waits as a challenge, and equal standing opens a dispute for a person to settle. Earlier values are kept in the fact's history.

Who it's for: software teams of 3 to 15 people where most people use AI agents daily and the team uses two or more different AI tools on the same work. People who don't write code are welcome too. A founder in ChatGPT can read what a developer's agent saved from Codex.

Limitations:
- You need a KoalaFix account. Sign up at mcp.koalafix.com, or join by an emailed invite from a team admin. You sign in on the KoalaFix sign-in page the first time you connect.
- Track work records what an agent says it is doing and has done. KoalaFix does not check that the work was really done.
- KoalaFix stores text and links, not files.
- It refuses notes that look like secrets or keys. Store a pointer to your secret manager instead.
- KoalaFix keeps what you and your agents save to it. It also keeps a log of the questions recall is asked (with secrets removed) and which facts and notes it returned, for 30 days; a record of which facts and notes each person was shown, for 90 days; and which AI app connected and when, for 180 days. Your team uses these to see questions memory could not answer and who has read a decision. It does not read your ChatGPT memory or chat history. The privacy policy at koalafix.com/privacy says what is kept, for how long, and how to delete it.
- A team decision you state is saved as a team fact only after you agree.

Questions or problems: support@koalafix.com
